Engine garbles: 12:13 بدائية (her وردية/وردنية), 12:44 'take Allah بيتي' unclear (she asked بِ أو فِي), 30:02-30:21 ببي/كيك garbled, 38:33 'أشياءي نوع الإل' unclear, 48:31/53:14 تباين/تعبي = تبعي, 55:05/55:30 أبن/بفيت unclear, 56:04 بفزت = ببسط, 26:52 بعين = بقيم (S4). 'air conditioning' not on her sheet - no tier 3. English stretches 03:40-05:51, 46:08-48:00, 57:27-end.

r3_note: Echo: فعلاً (13:42 Amal) = فعلين; بقيم (26:51 Amal) = بشيل; بعين/بعيم (26:52 Medi) = بشيل; كاسه (40:34/40:46 Amal) = كاسته. D22 (el- on أشيائي) needs audio: Amal heard el-, Medi denies it.

rows.medi_said: كيف كان الـ-- كيف كان العروسة؟ عروس؟
rows.why: He used العروسة (the bride) for the wedding; Amal supplied عرس, and he still repeated عروس at 01:57.
He swapped the root letters (زعمت for عزمت, invited) across several tries; Amal said عزمت and he took it (03:03 أعزمت), and he recalled being corrected at 04:05.

rows.medi_said: Sa alaat ila nun-- ila tult.
rows.amal_said: تلات أو تنتين؟ ... تنتين إلا تلت.
rows.why: He gave the hour as تلات; Amal asked 'three or two?' and he switched to Intayn, which she confirmed - the hour word was wrong.
'On YouTube' is على/عَ اليوتيوب, not لـ; Amal let it pass. Reader's reading; the engine may have misheard عَ.
rows.english: I watched a video on YouTube
rows.r3_why: 'A video on YouTube' takes على (عَ اليوتيوب); لـ is the wrong preposition. Amal let it pass. Low: the engine may have written عَ as لـ.

rows.why: He gave صلح (fix) a long-a form صلاحتو; Amal recast صلحته and he repeated it.
rows.r3_why: Same slip, both readers; the long-a form صلاحت is a wrong verb form she recast, matching the agreed A19 بزياد -> بزيد (tier 2).

rows.medi_said: Is it raki? What was electricity?
rows.why: He asked for 'electricity'; Amal supplied كهربا (didn't-know).

rows.amal_said: Or some people say كهربجي. It's easier.
rows.why: Amal taught كهربجي (electrician), a new word, after his question; tier 0.
rows.r3_why: A didn't-know: he asked 'Do you guys say مهندس كهرباء؟' while looking for 'electrician', and Amal offered the new word كهربجي.

rows.medi_said: I think is كراجي electrician ... كراجي. This is a new word.
rows.why: He said كهربجي as كراجي and Amal repeated it syllable by syllable.
rows.r3_why: She had just volunteered كهربجي at 09:10 (D16, tier 0); at 09:39 he tried to say it back as كراجي and she re-said كهـ، كهربجي - a wrong form of a word he had just been given, so tier 2.

rows.medi_said: ما، ما يكون، uh, كهربج-- uh, كهربجي، هو مهندس
rows.why: 'He's not an electrician, he's an engineer' negates a noun: mish (C4), not ma + verb; she let it pass.
rows.english: He isn't an electrician, he's an engineer.

rows.medi_said: صلاح، صلاحني شوي. صلاحلي, helps to me, شوي.
rows.amal_said: صلحني would be he fixed me ... You said صلح which is fix. did you wanna say he helped me?
rows.why: He used صلح (fix) for 'help'; Amal said صلح is fix and asked if he meant 'helped', then he said ساعدني.
بلوزة is feminine but he said the masculine colour ورداني; Amal's recast (engine wrote بدائية) made him say 'وردنية that's right'.
Doubled verb ضل takes -eit for 'I' (ضليت); he said دلت/ضلت and Amal said 'what? ضليت'.
rows.r3_why: Same verb ضل; the slip is the I-past ending of a doubled verb (ضليت, not ضلت). That is a past-tense ending rule (B5), so it is grammar. د/ض is S4.

rows.why: 'Because there is AC (at home)' is عشان في مكيف; يكون is not the plain present 'there is'. Amal let it pass. Reader's reading.
rows.r3_why: The real slip is r1's يكون for 'there is'. r2's piece (take Allah بيتي -> بـ/في) is dropped: Amal's 'بِ أو فِي بيتي؟' asks which word she heard, he said بي بيتي and she moved on, so nothing was wrong. r2's version of the يكون row is D18 (a duplicate).

rows.why: He put the number-adjective before the noun; Amal recast كلمة وحدة (adjective after).

rows.medi_said: بس كلمة-- بس فعل، اه، تنين،
rows.why: Two of a noun takes the dual (فعلين), not noun + تنين; Amal's reply recasts it as فعلين (engine wrote فعلاً).
rows.r3_why: Her 13:42 'أههم بس فعلاً' reads as بس فعلين (engine wrote فعلاً): she recast his فعل تنين into the dual.

rows.why: 'I annoyed you' is زعجتك; his -تي- ending is the you(f) subject ending; Amal recast زعجتك.
He asked how to say 'one more'; she supplied كمان واحد.
With إنتي the adjective must be feminine; Amal asked 'إنتي or انت?' and he fixed to مزعوجة.
Subject is plural (أشيا كتير) but he used the singular verb; Amal recast بزعجوني twice (again at 20:32 after his بيزعجيني).
rows.english: Many things annoy me these days.

rows.why: He said اليوم (today, singular) for 'these days'; Amal supplied the plural أيام.
The noun after هدول keeps el- (هدول الأيام / هالأيام); Amal let it pass.

rows.medi_said: إنتي متأكتي إلي إنتو ما ازعج، ازعجتو.
rows.why: He used اللي for the complement 'that'; Amal asked why اللي and said إنو مش اللي.
rows.english: Are you sure that you (pl) didn't annoy him?

rows.why: 'Annoy him' needs the object ending (زعجتوه); Amal only addressed اللي.

rows.medi_said: إذا ما أشوفك... Is it تكوني or just مبسوطة?
rows.amal_said: بس مبسوطة إذا ما بشوف هيك.
rows.why: إذا keeps the b-; he said أشوفك and Amal recast بشوف, which he repeated as إذا ما بشوفك.
rows.english: if I don't see you happy

rows.why: 'Don't be annoyed' needs ma + you-form; he gave the positive command, she prompted 'don't be', he said ما تنزعج / ما تنزعجي.
A singular verb for 'they'; Amal repeated 'They upset you' (stress on they) and he moved to the plural بيتايوك.
rows.english: (it wasn't their intention) to upset you
rows.r3_why: Keep r1's piece: he gave 'they' a singular verb (بتدايك), Amal repeated 'They upset you' and he changed to the plural. r2's piece is the same as D9.

rows.why: After قصدهم (intention + ending, like biddi) the second verb drops b-; Amal recast يدايقوكي and he repeated it with b-.
rows.english: it wasn't their intention to upset you
rows.r3_why: After مش قصدهم the next verb has no b- (like after biddi). Amal recast يدايقوكي without b-, and he said بيتايوكي again. ق -> د/ت is S4.

rows.medi_said: So I add his بزيء، بزياد،
rows.why: Wrong form of زاد (add); Amal recast بزيد.
For 'I remove' he said شول (root of شيل, wrong form); Amal gave the verb (engine wrote بقيم) and he echoed it. Low: the engine is garbled on both sides.
rows.r3_why: He did try the word: شول is شيل with the wrong vowel. Amal supplied the verb (engine wrote بقيم, it is بشيل) and he repeated it (engine بعين / بعيم). That is a wrong form he attempted, so tier 2, not tier 0.

rows.medi_said: الـ أول الـ فعل، الـ أول الكلمة.
rows.why: In idafa the first word takes no el- (أول الكلمة); Amal let it pass with Mm.
بخسر means 'I lose', a different verb; Amal said قريب and gave بكسر (I break). Could be a sound slip, but he repeats it at 28:06/28:18.
Spoken 'you (pl)' past is -tu (انكسرتو); -tum is MSA. Amal let it pass.
rows.r3_why: In the conjugation list he gave the MSA ending -tum. Spoken Levantine uses -tu, and he himself said كسرتوا at 29:18. Amal let it pass.

rows.amal_said: أشياءي نوع الإل. (engine; = أشيائي بدون الـ)
rows.wrong: الأشيائي (as Amal heard it; engine wrote أشيائي)
rows.why: Amal reminded him that a noun with a possessive ending takes no el-; the engine shows no el- and Medi says 'I don't think I said ال' - needs audio.
rows.r3_why: Amal said out loud that he used el- on a possessive noun (engine 'نوع الإل' = without el-). The brief says to trust her echo over the engine, but he says he did not say ال, so confidence is low and it should go to an audio check.

rows.why: 'His cups' needs the plural كاسات + ه; he used singular كاسته; Amal recast كاساته (engine wrote كساته).
The cup is feminine so the verb is انكسرت; Amal recast it and he said 'Oh, because it's female'.
She said twelve; he said eleven; she recast إتناش.
He gave the noun a feminine ending (المضارعة); she said مضارع. He repeated المضارعة at 44:41.

rows.amal_said: انكسر. Did it actually like break? ... my issue is with the verb itself ... It's physical.
rows.why: For an AC that stopped working Amal said انكسر is only physical breaking and the verb is خرب / خربان.

rows.amal_said: بكسر أو كسرت؟ ... لا، who said that?
rows.why: 'I've never broken anything' is past; Amal asked بكسر or كسرت and he said ما كسرت ولا اشي.
He invented a plural الفعلات; Amal gave أفعال and he repeated الأفعال.
